frameworks.name: Enterprise Lead Generation Architecture
frameworks.definition: A three-tier system combining cold outbound, event-based acquisition, and affiliate partnerships, where outbound feeds event attendance and events surface both direct deals and affiliate partners.

frameworks.name: Affiliate Activation Strategy
frameworks.definition: Treating affiliates as a second customer base requiring dedicated success cadences and data-driven diagnostics to identify and replicate behaviors of high-performing partners.

claims.text: When a consulting firm's largest vertical (banking) experiences a crisis and demand disappears, successful founders pivot to where supply is available, maintaining revenue-generating capability across industries through leveraging industry-agnostic service disciplines.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Supply-constrained verticals disappear; founder quickly reallocates to adjacent verticals where the core capability (data management, risk, regulatory change) remains applicable, preserving the revenue stream.
bounded_by: Assumes core capability is transferable across industries
Does not apply to industry-specific service models

claims.text: Founder-led sales, while effective at lower scales, becomes a constraint on growth; founders who have demonstrated multi-figure professional services sales can scale further by systematizing lead generation rather than relying on founder relationships and texting.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: aiming to scale beyond founder capacity
claims.mechanism: Founder personal network and relationship management do not scale linearly; systematizing lead sources (events, cold outbound, affiliate deals) decouples revenue from founder availability.
bounded_by: Does not apply to relationship-dependent advisory where founder credibility is the entire offer

claims.text: For enterprise services sales, the acquisition funnel is constraint-gated at lead volume: once onboarding, delivery, finance, and operations are systematized (scored 8/9), the binding bottleneck shifts to sales and marketing, specifically to increasing leads flowing into an already-effective close process.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Presumes sales/close mechanics are already effective

claims.text: For enterprise-level sales, attending 10-20 trade shows or conferences per year is suboptimal; the multiplier effect of events (direct deals + affiliate identification + warm outbound targeting) justifies significantly higher attendance volume (200+ events annually).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Each event surfaces multiple parallel acquisition channels—direct closing from stage, identification of potential affiliate partners, and generation of warm outbound targets—compounding the ROI per event.
bounded_by: Founder must be capable of closing from stage

claims.text: When an enterprise sales organization has many affiliate partners but they are not actively referring business, the underlying problem is not partner quality but partner activation—lack of a dedicated success function and regular cadenced communication to replicate high-performer behaviors.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Partners need quantified feedback (which partner demographics and behaviors drive referrals), regular cadenced outreach, and success support; without this, even good partners remain dormant due to lack of attention and clarity on expected behaviors.
bounded_by: Assumes partner network quality is adequate

claims.text: Affiliates should be treated as a second customer base requiring dedicated customer success infrastructure (regular cadence communication, success metrics tracking, behavioral diagnostics) to identify and replicate the actions of high-performing partners across the entire network.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: For software companies with multi-tier customers (SMBs, agencies, agency influencers), the leverage point is not SMBs directly but agencies as the operator layer, and super-affiliates as the distribution layer—structuring the product, pricing, and success efforts around these leverage tiers enables exponential scaling.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Agencies become the primary customer because they service SMBs; super-affiliates become the distribution force because they command hundreds/thousands of agencies. Success investment in these tiers compounds.

anchors.value: 500-1,000+ agencies in network; one email reaches 100-500 agencies

bounded_by: Requires agencies to be the actual operator/reseller, not just customer

claims.text: The three-part enterprise lead generation system combines cold outbound (to source event opportunities and affiliate deals), physical event attendance (to close deals directly and identify partners), and affiliate partnership (to provide ongoing lead flow between events), creating a reinforcing acquisition loop where each channel feeds the others.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not apply to SMB/low-touch sales
Requires founder/sales leader to be present at events and able to close from stage

claims.text: When lead volume is the constraint, constraining focus to the three highest-leverage acquisition sources (events, cold outbound, affiliates) and executing them with a documented playbook at scale is more effective than experimenting with many lead sources simultaneously.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: lead volume is the binding constraint
other functions (sales, delivery, operations) are mature
claims.mechanism: Depth in a few channels compounds (playbook refinement, repeatability, compounding returns from events and affiliates); breadth in many channels divides focus and prevents playbook development.

examples.text: Sharron, CEO/president of a publicly traded real estate brokerage company, grew the firm from $200M to $1.2B by executing a single lever: attending 220 speaking events per year, closing directly from stage with every person who approached him. This demonstrates the multiplier effect of event-based sales for enterprise-level businesses.

Eclipse Consulting's managing partner faced a vertical concentration risk when banking clients (Credit Suisse, Silicon Valley Bank) were hit by financial crisis, causing firm revenue to drop from $30M+ to $15M. Rather than specializing further, he pivoted the entire firm to adjacent regulated verticals (asset management, insurance, private equity) where the core competency (data management, risk, regulatory advisory) remained applicable, enabling recovery and trajectory toward $100M by 2029.

Eclipse Consulting built a robust alliance partner framework with many affiliate partners, but found that most were not activating—not sending referral business despite being in the network. The issue was not partner selection but partner neglect: partners lacked regular cadenced communication, success metrics feedback, and clarity on behavioral expectations. Implementing affiliate customer success (regular communication, quantified diagnostics, behavioral replication) would activate dormant partners.

At a prior software company, the founder initially thought SMBs were the primary customer, but discovered that agencies were the actual operator layer serving SMBs. The company then restructured product, pricing, and success efforts around agencies as the primary customer. Upon further scale, they identified super-affiliates (individuals/entities managing 500-1,000 agencies) who could push the product to hundreds of agencies with one email, warranting a third tier of success infrastructure.

practices.text: When lead generation is the binding constraint, document and execute a repeatable playbook for event attendance, cold outbound, and affiliate deal-making rather than experimenting with many tactics.

For each affiliate partner tier, implement a dedicated success cadence including regular communication, quantified feedback on referral-driving demographics and behaviors, and behavioral diagnostics to identify replicable high-performer patterns.

In enterprise sales, aim for significant volume of event attendance (100+ annually) to maximize the compounding effect of direct closes, affiliate identification, and warm outbound pipeline generation per event.
